PART 10 THERMOSETTING Section PROPERTIES Temperature of 4 Determination of Gel Time and Peak Exothermic Reacting Thermosetting Resins

FOREWORD This Indian Standard (part 10/Sec 4) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Methods of Test for Plastics Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. The method prescribed in this standard is operatordependent determining conditions required to produce an end product. since it is simple to perform. It is of value for

Since the gel time and the peak exotherrnic temperature of a reacting thermosetting plastics composition vary with the volume of material mixed at one time, it is essential that the volume be specified in any determination. By selection of an appropriate volume, gel time and peak exothermic data may be obtained in sufficiently precise and reproducible form or application evaluation, quality control, and material characterization of a thermosetting plastic composition. For most meaningful results, the cross sectional area of the material being examined, as well as other conditions of testing, should appro~'mate as closely as possible the conditions of use of the material. While preparing this standard considerable assistance has been derived from ASTM D 2471-94 `Standard test method for Gel Time and Peak Exotheric Temperature of Reacting Termosetting Resins' issued by American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM), USA. In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2: 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'.

PART 10 THERMOSETTING

4 Determination of Gel Time and Peak Exothermic Reacting Thermosetting Resins

1 SCOPE This standard (Part 10/Sec 4) prescribes the method for the determination of the time from the initial mixing of the reactants of a thcrmosetting plastic composition to the time when solidification commences, under conditions approximating the conditions of use. This method also provides a means for measuring the maximum temperature reached by a reacting thermosetting plastic composition, as well as (he time from initial mixing to the time when this peak exothermic temperature is reached. This test method is limited to reacting mixtures exhibiting gel times greater than 5 minutes. 2 APPARATUS
2.1 Sample Containers, contain a volume of reacting

at least 4 h prior to being tested, or for however much longer time is needed for all parts of the sample to reach the test temperature within 0.5�C. Condition all containers and probes to be used in the test at the test temperature at the same time. 3.2 If experience has shown that less than 4 h conditioning is required for all parts of the sample to reach the test temperature, report the time of condhioning. 4 PROCEDURE 4.1 When all components have reached the test temperature agitate each component slowly and separately with a stirring rod or mixing paddle for at least 3 minutes, avoiding the entrapment of air.
NOTE -- The test temperature shall be 27 f 2�C unless otherwise specified.

4.3 Start the stop watch, and mix the components thoroughly for 3 minutes, avoiding air entrapment by slow agitation with a stirring rod or mixing paddle. To avoid transfer of heat, do not hold the container by hand during the tnixing operation. Record the start of mixing as the `starting time'. 4.4 Transfer the appropriate test volume (see Note ) of the mixed components immediately to an appropriate sample container which has been previously conditioned at the test temperature. 4.5 Place the sample container on a nonconducting surface in still air at the test temperature.
NOTE -- If it is desirable, because of the nature of the appticati~ to use a conducting surface of high heat capacity instead of a nonconducting surface, include a description of the surface in the report. Ifi because of the nature of an application, it becomes desirable to measure gel time and peak exotbermic temperature in a temperature controlled bath, the conditions used shall be noted in the report.

4.8 When the reacting material no longer adheres to the end of a clean probe, record the `gel time' as the elapsed time from the start of mixing. 4.9 Continue reeording the time and temperature until the temperature starts to drop. Record the highest temperature reached as the `peak exothermic temperature'. Record the `peak exothermic time' as the elapsed time from the start of mixing. 5 REPORT

Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards: Monthly Additions'.
